body:
Native Windows qualification exposed failures in credential replacement, retained-directory export, Task Scheduler definition comparison, and uninstall timing. Fix those paths, protect saved prompt records with owner-only ACLs, and move the tray status color to the outer shape so it is easier to see.

Replace Unix-only test assumptions with native Windows fixtures, correct the real modal-menu tests, and require the relevant Windows regressions in CI. The qualification receipt records host details, artifact hashes, observed results, and remaining evidence requirements: [Windows native qualification](https://github.com/InkyQuill/hieronymus/blob/c82fb7a1eb04a545a0b5431379a1ed4211f02ed5/docs/desktop-windows-native-2026-09-12.md).

Validation on Windows x64/MSVC:

- Required fmt, Clippy and rustdoc checks passed; script tests: 100 passed; frontend typecheck, 85 tests and build passed.
- CLI library: 120 passed; private files: 5 passed; native desktop: 5 passed; uninstall: 4 passed; icon rendering: 7 passed; both ignored native modal tests passed.
- Real packaged ONNX inference, authenticated MCP and graceful shutdown passed. A distinct compiled stopped-instance update, injected unhealthy-candidate rollback, and separate packaged uninstall passed. User confirmed Explorer recovery and improved status-color visibility.
- The full Rust suite remains environmentally inconclusive: the final run stopped at three loopback connection resets. An earlier full no-fail-fast run also captured AdGuard-modified HTTP responses. Network assertions remain intact and networking settings were left alone as requested.

This is source qualification, not release promotion. Active-daemon upgrade attempts safely refused under unreliable loopback connectivity; fresh logon, the full appearance/DPI matrix, native agent-host acceptance and canonical CI model-archive provenance remain unqualified. Windows returned the rebuilt helper to tray overflow, so always-visible preference persistence is also not established. The project version remains 0.9.0; 0.9.1-qualification was only an ignored local compiled fixture.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Improved reliability of private credential and prompt-file replacement on Windows, including safer handling when files are in use.
  - Windows broker operations now verify successful child-process completion before reporting success.
  - Improved Windows export and Task Scheduler handling for more dependable file and service operations.
  - Corrected platform-specific installer, update, uninstall, and lifecycle behavior across Windows, macOS, and Linux.

- **Documentation**
  - Expanded Windows qualification guidance and recorded native validation results, limitations, and remaining checks.
